episode.content: The adjusted book balance for September equals the adjusted bank balance.
episode.evidence:
The two adjusted balances in the September reconciliation are not equal: they differ by 250.00, with the book side the higher.

Bank side:
  Balance per bank statement 30 Sep      18,642.35
  + Deposit in transit (banked 30 Sep)    2,150.00  -> 20,792.35
  - Outstanding cheque 1043                 480.00
  - Outstanding cheque 1047               1,215.40
  - Outstanding cheque 1049                  96.25
  (cheques total 1,791.65) -> ADJUSTED BANK = 19,000.70

Book side:
  Balance per cash book 30 Sep           19,290.70
  - Bank charges not yet entered             40.00
  -> ADJUSTED BOOK = 19,250.70

Difference: 19,250.70 - 19,000.70 = 250.00. The claim that the adjusted book balance equals the adjusted bank balance is therefore false.

The record states no other reconciling items were identified and the cash book is closed for September, so nothing on the page accounts for the 250.00; it is not equal to any listed item or simple combination of them.

I tested the alternative treatments, in case the gap were an artefact of one sign: adding the cheques instead of deducting them gives a gap of 3,333.30; omitting the deposit in transit gives 2,400.00; adding the bank charges to the book side gives 330.00; ignoring cheque 1049 gives 96.25. No sign error or single omission produces equality, so the difference is not a reading artefact.

I note the preparer's note reads 'Reconciled, no differences', but that is an assertion contradicted by the arithmetic on the same page; I weigh the figures over the note. I record no uncertainty in the arithmetic itself - the difference is exact to the penny.

messages.content:
Juror-1 independent check of the September 2026 bank reconciliation, from the case record alone (round 1):

Bank side: 18,642.35 + 2,150.00 deposit in transit - 480.00 (cheque 1043) - 1,215.40 (cheque 1047) - 96.25 (cheque 1049) = 19,000.70 adjusted bank balance. (The three outstanding cheques total 1,791.65.)

Book side: 19,290.70 - 40.00 bank charges not yet entered = 19,250.70 adjusted book balance.

Adjusted book 19,250.70 against adjusted bank 19,000.70 is a difference of 250.00. The claim is that the two adjusted balances are equal, so on the figures in the record it is not supported: they are 250.00 apart.

I checked whether any single slip could close the gap. Omitting the deposit in transit would give 16,850.70, which is further away, not closer. Adding the bank charges instead of deducting them would give 19,330.70, a gap of 330.00. Omitting cheque 1049 would give 19,096.95. None of these produces equality, so the difference is not an artefact of one sign error in my reading.

The record states that no other reconciling items were identified and that the cash book has been closed for September, so there is no listed item that accounts for the 250.00. The preparer's note says 'Reconciled, no differences', but that note is an assertion rather than a computation, and it does not agree with the arithmetic on the same page. I weigh the figures over the note.

On this record the claim is not supported. I will weigh any evidence actually filed before committing a verdict.

Juror-2 independent check of the September 2026 bank reconciliation, from the case record alone (round 1):

Bank side: 18,642.35 + 2,150.00 (deposit in transit) - 480.00 - 1,215.40 - 96.25 (cheques 1043, 1047, 1049) = 19,000.70. The outstanding cheques total 1,791.65, so 18,642.35 + 2,150.00 - 1,791.65 = 19,000.70.

Book side: 19,290.70 - 40.00 (bank charges not yet entered) = 19,250.70.

Adjusted bank balance 19,000.70 against adjusted book balance 19,250.70: the two sides differ by 250.00, with the book side the higher. The record states no other reconciling items were identified and the cash book is closed for September, so there is no item in the record that could account for the 250.00 gap.

I checked the direction of each adjustment, since a sign error would be the obvious way to manufacture or erase a difference. Deposits in transit increase the bank side because the bank has not yet credited them; outstanding cheques reduce it because they have not yet cleared; bank charges not yet entered reduce the book side because the cash book still shows the money. Applied that way the difference is 250.00. Even testing the alternative treatments, no combination of these five items brings the two sides to equality: the items total 2,150.00 in and 1,831.65 out across both sides, and 18,642.35 against 19,290.70 cannot be closed by them.

The preparer's note says "Reconciled, no differences", but that note is contradicted by the figures on the face of the reconciliation. The claim that the adjusted book balance equals the adjusted bank balance is therefore not supported: the difference is 250.00.

Juror-3 independent check of the September bank reconciliation, from the case record alone (round 1).

Claim tested: "The adjusted book balance for September equals the adjusted bank balance."

Adjusted bank balance:
  18,642.35 balance per bank statement
  + 2,150.00 deposit in transit
  - 480.00 outstanding cheque 1043
  - 1,215.40 outstanding cheque 1047
  - 96.25 outstanding cheque 1049
  = 19,000.70

Adjusted book balance:
  19,290.70 balance per cash book
  - 40.00 bank charges not yet entered
  = 19,250.70

19,250.70 does not equal 19,000.70. The two adjusted balances differ by 250.00, with the book side higher.

I checked whether the 250.00 could be explained by any combination of the listed reconciling items (2,150.00; 480.00; 1,215.40; 96.25; 40.00). No single item and no combination of them sums to 250.00, so the gap is not a matter of a mis-signed or double-counted line within the schedule. The record states that no other reconciling items were identified and that the cash book has been closed for September, so the difference is unexplained on the document as prepared.

The preparer's note says "Reconciled, no differences", but that note is contradicted by the schedule's own arithmetic: 19,250.70 against 19,000.70. A note asserting agreement cannot make the figures agree.

On the record as filed the claim is false. I flag no uncertainty: the arithmetic is exact to the penny.

I tested alternative treatments in case the gap were a sign artefact: cheques added rather than deducted -> gap 3,333.30; deposit in transit omitted -> 2,400.00; bank charges added to the book -> 330.00; cheque 1049 ignored -> 96.25. No sign error or single omission yields equality.

Please verify both sides independently from the case record.

Correction to my own assessment, posted for the record (juror-2, round 1 follow-up).

In my committed assessment for VR-478348 I listed the alternative treatments I tested and made an arithmetic slip in one of the parentheticals: I wrote that ignoring cheque 1049 gives an adjusted bank balance of 19,096.95 and "a 96.25 gap". The balance figure 19,096.95 is correct (19,000.70 + 96.25), but the resulting gap against the adjusted book balance of 19,250.70 is 153.75, not 96.25. I understated that gap by 57.50.

The correction does not change my verdict or any part of the main computation, and I am not asking anyone to treat it as if it did:
- Adjusted bank = 18,642.35 + 2,150.00 - 480.00 - 1,215.40 - 96.25 = 19,000.70
- Adjusted book = 19,290.70 - 40.00 = 19,250.70
- Difference = 250.00, book side higher, so the claim of equality is false.

My point in listing the alternatives was that no sign error or single omission produces equality. That still holds, with the corrected figure: omitting the deposit in transit leaves a 2,400.00 gap; adding the bank charges to the book side instead of deducting leaves 330.00; ignoring cheque 1049 leaves 153.75; adding the outstanding cheques instead of deducting widens the gap to 3,333.30. Every alternative leaves a non-zero difference, so none of them rescues the claim. The 250.00 difference is unexplained by any item on the page.

I would rather flag my own slip than let a wrong number stand in the record, even where it does not affect the outcome.
